nodes.description: MEGF10 and Notch1 interact through their respective intracellular domains, and the interaction is lost with the p.Cys774Arg allele. Silencing Megf10 in MyoD-null myoblasts lowers Notch and Hes1 transcript levels, so the receptor acts on Notch signalling that normally restrains terminal myogenic differentiation. Sertraline, which corrects the cellular phenotype of several disease models, also restores Notch1 in them. MEGF10 is one of three muscle disease genes that act on this pathway, alongside the Notch ligand JAG2 and POGLUT1, which glycosylates the Notch receptor ectodomain.

nodes.description: MEGF10 is a transmembrane receptor with 17 atypical EGF-like repeats whose conserved cysteines form disulfide bonds; it marks quiescent satellite cells and is expressed in myoblasts but not in differentiated myofibers. The pathogenic cysteine substitutions p.Cys326Arg and p.Cys774Arg reduce tyrosine phosphorylation of the receptor, and the principal site, Y1030, is required for the proliferative effect of MEGF10 on myoblasts, so the receptor loses its signalling output rather than merely being absent from the surface.

nodes.description: A second site of pathology, demonstrated so far only in the mouse. MEGF10 concentrates at the neuromuscular junction postnatally and is enriched in perisynaptic Schwann cells; Megf10 knockout mice develop early and progressive junctional degeneration with postsynaptic fragmentation, presynaptic regions not covered by acetylcholine receptors and perisynaptic Schwann cell processes entering the synaptic cleft, and the diaphragm is affected earliest. evidence.snippet: In contrast to previously reported EMARDD patients, her weakness was more prominent proximally than distally, and involved her legs more than her arms.

evidence.reference_title: Unmasking MEGF10 Myopathy: A Rare Cause of Sudden Respiratory Failure in a Young Adult.
evidence.snippet: Physical examination showed symmetrical proximal paresis in arms and legs (MRC 4/5), dependence on hand support for head lifting, and inability to rise from a squat unaided.

nodes.description: The consequence of the stem cell defect at tissue level: fewer myofibers are formed and damaged muscle is repaired poorly. Megf10 knockout mice have fewer fibers and smaller muscles as juveniles and adults and regenerate poorly after repeated barium chloride injury, and the multinucleated myofibers formed by satellite cell fusion are greatly reduced in patient muscle. The overload experiments show that the hypertrophic response is also lost, so growth as well as repair is affected.
nodes.id: Reduced Myofiber Number and Impaired Muscle Regeneration

evidence.reference_title: Cellular and molecular alterations to muscles and neuromuscular synapses in a mouse model of MEGF10-related myopathy.
evidence.snippet: Consistent with the TA in young adult Megf10 KO mice having fewer muscle fibers, the TA mass is smaller in Megf10 KO mice compared to control mice (Fig. 1D-E).

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in MEGF10, a regulator of satellite cell myogenesis, cause early onset myopathy, areflexia, respiratory distress and dysphagia (EMARDD).
evidence.snippet: MEGF10 is highly expressed in activated satellite cells and regulates their proliferation as well as their differentiation and fusion into multinucleated myofibers, which are greatly reduced in muscle from individuals with early onset myopathy, areflexia, respiratory distress and dysphagia.

nodes.description: Megf10-null satellite cells and myoblasts proliferate and migrate less than wild-type cells, and the same defect follows short hairpin knockdown of Megf10 or overexpression of the human p.Cys774Arg allele in C2C12 cells. Reduced migration matters because satellite cells must travel to the site of damage before fusing.
nodes.id: Reduced Satellite Cell Proliferation and Migration

animal_models.description: Satellite cells isolated from the knockout show the proliferation and migration defects directly.
animal_models.name: Megf10 knockout mouse

evidence.reference_title: Megf10 deficiency impairs skeletal muscle stem cell migration and muscle regeneration.
evidence.snippet: Megf10-/- muscle satellite cells showed reduced proliferation and migration, while Megf10-/- mouse skeletal muscles showed impaired regeneration.

evidence.reference_title: Consequences of MEGF10 deficiency on myoblast function and Notch1 interactions.
evidence.snippet: We demonstrate that short hairpin RNA (shRNA)-mediated knockdown of Megf10, as well as overexpression of the pathogenic human p.C774R mutation, leads to impaired proliferation and migration of C2C12 cells.

evidence.reference_title: Genetic disruption of satellite cell function underlying congenital myopathies.
evidence.snippet: Loss-of-function variants in MEGF10, which mediates satellite cell proliferation, result in early-onset myopathy characterized by severe weakness and areflexia.

experimental_models.name: Patient iPSC-derived myoblasts and Megf10-null mouse myoblasts in a small molecule screen

nodes.description: The defining and life-limiting feature. In the severe form respiratory failure begins in the first months of life and leads to long-term ventilation; in the mild variant it appears in the second decade or later, and in several adults it was the presenting problem. Nearly half of reported patients are described as dying after progression to long-term respiratory support.
nodes.id: Respiratory insufficiency due to muscle weakness

evidence.reference_title: Large phenotypic variability with severe respiratory involvement in MEGF10-related myopathies: Description of three cases.
evidence.snippet: The main clinical features included generalized hypotonia, respiratory insufficiency due to diaphragmatic involvement, and feeding difficulties.

evidence.reference_title: Phenotypic Variability of MEGF10 Variants Causing Congenital Myopathy: Report of Two Unrelated Patients from a Highly Consanguineous Population.
evidence.snippet: With progression of the disease, respiratory failure necessitates long term respiratory support, with subsequent demise of nearly half of the patients.

evidence.reference_title: Adult-onset respiratory insufficiency, scoliosis, and distal joint hyperlaxity in patients with multiminicore disease due to novel Megf10 mutations.
evidence.snippet: We report 2 sisters with adult-onset respiratory insufficiency followed by development of limb weakness.

nodes.description: Rimmed vacuoles with protein aggregates instead of minicores, reported in three adult-onset patients from two families and resembling a myofibrillar myopathy.

evidence.reference_title: Expanded spectrum of MEGF10 related myopathies: late-onset myofibrillar myopathy-like phenotype with novel variants.
evidence.snippet: Muscle pathology was characterized by rimmed vacuoles, and abnormal protein aggregates rather than minicores.

nodes.description: Scoliosis from axial weakness, frequently severe and often requiring spinal fusion. It can be the presenting complaint, including in school-age children whose myopathy had not been suspected, and it aggravates the restrictive respiratory defect.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in the satellite cell gene MEGF10 cause a recessive congenital myopathy with minicores.
evidence.snippet: All three patients had childhood onset scoliosis and were treated with spinal fusion surgery, and beginning at age 10–11 years, they all developed respiratory problems treated with bilevel positive airway pressure ventilation at night.

evidence.reference_title: Severe Scoliosis As the Clue for an Early Onset Myopathy, Areflexia, Respiratory Distress, and Dysphagia (EMARDD) Diagnosis During Childhood: A Case Report.
evidence.snippet: We present a novel case of a school-aged boy with scoliosis and progressive muscle weakness, featuring new onset hypotonia and respiratory distress.

nodes.description: Surgical stabilization of the neuromuscular scoliosis, needed in childhood in many patients and sometimes repeatedly.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in the satellite cell gene MEGF10 cause a recessive congenital myopathy with minicores.
evidence.snippet: All three patients had childhood onset scoliosis and were treated with spinal fusion surgery, and beginning at age 10–11 years, they all developed respiratory problems treated with bilevel positive airway pressure ventilation at night.

evidence.reference_title: Novel SNP array analysis and exome sequencing detect a homozygous exon 7 deletion of MEGF10 causing early onset myopathy, areflexia, respiratory distress and dysphagia (EMARDD).
evidence.snippet: She has bladder incontinence and progressive scoliosis requiring numerous surgical stabilizations.

nodes.description: Minicores, seen as moth-eaten fibers on oxidative stains, in both fiber types. They are characteristic of the milder presentations and are absent in some patients, so biopsy cannot be used to exclude the diagnosis.
nodes.id: Type 1 and type 2 muscle fiber minicore regions

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in the satellite cell gene MEGF10 cause a recessive congenital myopathy with minicores.
evidence.snippet: NADH reductase histochemistry showed a “moth-eaten” appearance in fibers of both fiber types, indicative of minicores.

evidence.reference_title: Adult-onset respiratory insufficiency, scoliosis, and distal joint hyperlaxity in patients with multiminicore disease due to novel Megf10 mutations.
evidence.snippet: A biopsy of the right triceps muscle in 1 sister showed multiple minicore structures.

nodes.description: Facial weakness, in some patients amounting to facial diplegia.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in the satellite cell gene MEGF10 cause a recessive congenital myopathy with minicores.
evidence.snippet: Facial weakness was also evident.

evidence.reference_title: Phenotypic Variability of MEGF10 Variants Causing Congenital Myopathy: Report of Two Unrelated Patients from a Highly Consanguineous Population.
evidence.snippet: Additional features include dysphagia often requiring gastrostomy feeding, generalized muscle weakness causing delayed motor development, poor head control, facial weakness, cleft palate, contractures, and scoliosis

nodes.description: Four independent splice-site morpholinos against megf10, used to corroborate the pathogenicity of the human missense alleles. Morphants show curved tails, impaired motility and disorganized muscle tissue.

Novel homozygous missense allele at a cysteine of an EGF-like domain in a boy with the severe phenotype whose biopsy showed reduced Pax7-positive satellite cells. It is an example of early-onset disease with biallelic missense alleles, against the usual genotype to onset rule.

evidence.reference_title: Large phenotypic variability with severe respiratory involvement in MEGF10-related myopathies: Description of three cases.
evidence.snippet: Genetic studies disclosed the novel homozygous MEGF10 c.337T>C, p.(Cys113Arg) variant.

nodes.description: Compound heterozygous missense alleles in the family in which the minicore presentation was described. Both replace a conserved cysteine of an atypical EGF-like repeat and both reduce tyrosine phosphorylation of MEGF10 in vitro; p.Cys774Arg also disrupts the interaction with Notch1.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in the satellite cell gene MEGF10 cause a recessive congenital myopathy with minicores.
evidence.snippet: Affected subjects were compound heterozygous for missense mutations c.976T > C (p.C326R) and c.2320T > C (p.C774R).

evidence.reference_title: Cysteine mutations cause defective tyrosine phosphorylation in MEGF10 myopathy.
evidence.snippet: Two mutations in the extracellular EGF-like domains of MEGF10, C326R and C774R, were associated with decreased tyrosine phosphorylation of MEGF10 in vitro.
